status: Proposed research shortlist; no outreach sent
method: Public primary sources and author portfolios. Fit is an assessment. Unconfirmed relationship does not establish absence. No numeric candidate scores.

candidates.name: Steven Molotnikov
candidates.connection_detail: Cosmos’s grants page identifies Steven as the Priori builder and reports that he accepted a Cosmos Fellowship.
candidates.work: Priori exposes assumptions and value choices as adjustable controls. His portfolio dates the interface project to November–December 2025.
candidates.fit: A concrete interface for making AI defaults easier to inspect and contest; a strong starting point for a prototype review.
candidates.contribution: Walk through Priori and identify which user actions would demonstrate meaningful oversight.
candidates.question: What does the current Priori study already test, and where would this pilot add value?
candidates.gap: Current build and study status, available evidence, interest and capacity need confirmation.

candidates.name: Cathy Mengying Fang
candidates.connection_detail: Cosmos identifies Cathy as a fellow grantee collaborating with Steven on a study of Priori’s effects on autonomy.
candidates.work: Her public portfolio lists Priori: Deference by Design (ICML 2026 Workshop), alongside research on chatbot use and human behavior.
candidates.work_label: Research portfolio · Priori and human–AI studies
candidates.fit: Connects interface building with human-subject research; useful for separating perceived control from observable reasoning behavior.
candidates.contribution: Review measures, comparison conditions and study burden before a workshop becomes an experiment.
candidates.question: How would we distinguish an increase in perceived autonomy from improved evidence evaluation?
candidates.gap: Existing protocol and results have not been reviewed. Her contribution should complement the joint Priori work, not duplicate it.

candidates.name: Philipp Koralus
candidates.connection_detail: Cosmos’s team page lists Philipp as a Founding Fellow; its research page lists him with Oxford HAI Lab.
candidates.work: Reason and Inquiry: The Erotetic Theory (2023), listed on his research page, examines reasoning through the questions people pursue.
candidates.work_label: Reason and Inquiry · research and publications
candidates.fit: Can help specify what improved judgment means and why rejecting AI advice is not automatically rational.
candidates.contribution: Critique the conceptual definition and translate it into defensible behavioral indicators.
candidates.question: When is delegation a reasoned exercise of autonomy, and what observation would distinguish it from unreflective deference?
candidates.gap: Proposed reviewer role only; availability, priorities and participation are unconfirmed.

candidates.name: Advait Sarkar
candidates.connection_detail: No Cosmos relationship was established in the institutional pages, author material and targeted search reviewed for this shortlist. This does not establish absence of a relationship.
candidates.work: Co-author of a January 2026 preprint comparing cognitive-forcing interventions in AI-assisted writing. It distinguishes interventions users prefer from those that reduce overreliance.
candidates.work_label: Cognitive forcing for AI execution plans · 2026 preprint
candidates.fit: Directly relevant to testing reflection prompts and assumption review while measuring effort and performance separately.
candidates.contribution: Critique the interface comparison and help avoid using satisfaction as a proxy for good judgment.
candidates.question: Which minimal intervention would be worth testing, and under what task conditions might it fail?
candidates.gap: The cited study concerns writing plans; applicability to conflicting-claim evaluation needs testing. His site announces a Microsoft departure in October 2026; use current contact details.

candidates.name: Zana Buçinca
candidates.connection_detail: No Cosmos relationship was established in the institutional pages, author material and targeted search reviewed for this shortlist. Shared institutions or coauthors are not treated as Cosmos connections.
candidates.work: Co-author of To Trust or to Think (2021): cognitive forcing reduced overreliance in the study, with costs in user ratings and uneven benefits. Her portfolio also lists contrastive-explanation research (CHI 2025).
candidates.work_label: To Trust or to Think · 2021 paper
candidates.fit: A strong methodological counterweight to assuming that added friction helps every user; brings a focus on skill, burden and appropriate reliance.
candidates.contribution: Review failure conditions, participant differences and a later unaided reasoning measure.
candidates.question: Who might this intervention burden or fail to help, and how would we detect that?
candidates.gap: Results from specific decision tasks are not a general autonomy measure. Interest, availability and any existing Cosmos relationship remain unconfirmed.

candidates.name: Tianyi Alex Qiu
candidates.connection_detail: Cosmos lists Tianyi among current fellow projects and describes work on detecting and resolving contradictions to help users examine their own beliefs.
candidates.work: Co-author of The Lock-in Hypothesis: Stagnation by Algorithm (ICML 2025), studying belief reinforcement through models, simulations and usage data.
candidates.fit: Adds a technical perspective on belief revision and diversity beyond the immediate act of accepting or rejecting one answer.
candidates.contribution: Propose contradiction or belief-revision tasks that could complement an interface study.
candidates.question: Can we measure warranted belief revision without rewarding novelty, disagreement or contradiction for its own sake?
candidates.gap: Current tool readiness needs checking. Population-level lock-in evidence should not be treated as proof of individual autonomy gains.
